deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is an archival wrapper or envelope cover from the Göttingen library (Bibliotheca Regiae Academiae Georgiae Augustae). Its contents are:

- An oval ownership stamp reading 'EX BIBLIOTHECA REGIAE ACADEM. GEORGIAE AUG.'
- A handwritten accession number, '1897. 4658.'
- An ink label: 'Riemann'sche [inserted above the line] 3 Manuscripte von Ernst Schering und Abschrift eines Briefes von K. Schering.'
- A later pencil gloss in parentheses identifying K. Schering in relation to Ernst Schering.

The label means the bundle holds three Riemann manuscripts that came via Ernst Schering, plus a copy of a letter from K. Schering. Ernst Schering (1833–1897) was a Göttingen mathematician, Gauss editor and Riemann's colleague. The accession year 1897 is consistent with the bundle entering the library after his death in 1897. This is my inference.

The previous page is a report signed by H. Weber on the 'Hypothesen' manuscript. Together they suggest the bundle includes material related to Riemann's Habilitationsvortrag.

There is no derivation to reconstruct.

transcription_corrections: Stamp text should read in order: 'EX BIBLIOTHECA REGIAE ACADEM. GEORGIAE AUG.' The machine version scattered 'EX'.

'Riemann'sche' is an interlinear insertion with a caret placed before 'Manuscripte'. The intended reading is likely 'Riemann'sche Manuscripte' or '3 Riemann'sche Manuscripte', i.e. Riemann manuscripts from Ernst Schering's possession, not manuscripts authored by Schering.

The pencil line probably reads '(Sohns Moriz Schering, Bruders von Ernst Schering.)'. 'Moriz' is more likely than 'Moris', and 'Bruders' (genitive) fits the image. This reading is uncertain: the faint pencil makes the genealogical relation ambiguous.
